heading: Normalization
description:
Normalization organizes tables to minimize redundancy and dependency. Normal forms:

• 1NF — Atomic values, no repeating groups
• 2NF — 1NF + no partial dependencies
• 3NF — 2NF + no transitive dependencies
• BCNF — every determinant is a candidate key

Denormalization is sometimes used for read-heavy workloads to improve query performance at the cost of redundancy.

heading: SQL Joins & Queries
description:
Joins combine rows from two or more tables based on related columns.

Types of Joins:
• INNER JOIN — only matching rows
• LEFT JOIN — all from left + matching from right
• RIGHT JOIN — all from right + matching from left
• FULL OUTER JOIN — all rows from both tables
• CROSS JOIN — cartesian product
• SELF JOIN — table joined with itself

heading: Transactions & ACID Properties
description:
A transaction is a logical unit of work. ACID properties guarantee reliable processing:

• Atomicity — all or nothing
• Consistency — valid state transitions
• Isolation — concurrent transactions don't interfere
• Durability — committed data survives crashes

Isolation levels: Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable.
